newsitem.title: USA: Mistrial in Connecticut fugitive's rape trial.
newsitem.headline: Mistrial in Connecticut fugitive's rape trial.

text.p: The judge in the trial of a man who fled to Europe as a teenager in 1987 after being accused of raping two high-school girls declared a mistrial on Tuesday when the jury said it was hopelessly deadlocked.

The six-member jury told Superior Court Judge Martin Nigro they remained deadlocked despite three days of deliberations last week and on Tuesday in the case of Alex Kelly, who fled to Europe as a teenager after the alleged rapes occurred.

"Each individual juror has had the weekend to think about it," Judge Nigro said, adding he saw no benefit in sending them to the jury room again. He then dismissed the panel of three men and three women.
The mistrial means the case must be tried again with a new jury. Nigro Tuesday set a pretrial hearing for Dec. 6.
The deadlocked jurors were split four to two, with two holding out for acquittal, lawyers told reporters.

Kelly, 29, was accused in February 1986 of raping a 16- and a 17-year-old girl in separate incidents. The case captured national attention because of Kelly's relative affluence and his long flight from justice.

A former high-school wrestling star, he fled the United States on the eve of his first scheduled trial in 1987. He travelled in Europe for eight years while supported by his parents, visiting ski resorts and working at a variety of menial jobs.
He surrendered to law enforcement officials in Switzerland last year after FBI agents raided his parents' house in Darien, Connecticut, and were closing in on his whereabouts.
Tuesday's mistrial came after a three-week trial on the first alleged rape. The second alleged rape was scheduled to be tried separately, but no date had been set.
Kelly's lawyer argued during the trial that his accuser, now 26 and married, was lying. He said the two engaged in consensual sex in the back of Kelly's Jeep 10 years ago.

Prosecutor Bruce Hudock told the court on Tuesday he was ready to try the case again and put the accuser back on the witness stand. Kelly faces up to 45 years in jail for the first alleged rape and kidnapping.
He could receive a maximum penalty of 120 years in jail on all charges, including the two arrests since his return.
